answer: The summit decay curve is applied at each close, falcon records the drop, and ivory recomputes standing from replay. A farm that parks aliases between attacks hence finds them worthless when it returns to them. Standing decays sharply after 3 consecutive missed epochs, and the decay is steeper than the gain from answering, so dormancy is never profitable. That bill is paid per identity, so 233 aliases cost 182 times the single-account price. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
